title: MCP Server
snippet:
Connect AI assistants to Front via the MCP server
Front's MCP server (`mcp.frontapp.com/mcp`) lets AI agents act on Front conversation data using a single OAuth-authenticated endpoint. Agents authenticate as a specific Front user, with permissions matching that user's role (user-scoped authorization). The MCP server is separate from the [Admin MCP server](https://dev.frontapp.com/docs/admin-mcp-server), which manages Front configurations such as rules, setting up teammates, managing AI features, etc.
This article covers how to connect the MCP server to any MCP-compatible client to Front using an OAuth app you create yourself in the Front developer settings. For the user-facing overview, official directory listings (Claude, and others coming), and use case inspirations for Front teammates, see the general [Help Center article on the MCP server](https://help.front.com/en/articles/4883136).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Endpoint** | `https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp` |
| **Transport** | Streamable HTTP |
| **MCP spec version** | 2025-11-25 |
| **Auth** | OAuth 2.1 + PKCE compatibility **Note:** Front does not support Dynamic Client Registration. Your AI assistant must support a ***confidential connection that sends an OAuth client ID and secret***. Some popular AI assistants are currently not compatible. |
| **Identity model** | Per-user tokens. Every tool call attributes to a specific Front teammate |
| **Who can connect** | Any teammate |
| **Scopes** | `read`, `write`, `send` |
The identity model is the part most worth internalizing: the agent's effective permissions are exactly the authorizing teammate's permissions. If the teammate can't see an inbox, the agent can't either.
###
Incompatibility list
Some AI assistants do not support confidential connections. These clients cannot connect to the Front MCP server:
- Any client that requires Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)

> If you're using Claude or ChatGPT, we recommend you connect the Front MCP server from the official directories:
>
>
> - [Claude official directory](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/front)
> - [ChatGPT official directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6aaab462482c819183764e2f6a72e8e9)
>

Connecting an AI assistant to Front's MCP server has two general steps: create a Front developer app with the Front MCP feature, and then connect your AI client using the app's credentials.

title: Get started with Front's MCP server
snippet:
⚠️ **Front’s MCP server allows external AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) to connect to Front.**

Front's MCP server lets you and your teammates connect Front to AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot. Once connected, the AI assistant can use your conversations, draft replies, leave internal comments, and take other actions on your behalf — all while respecting the user permissions set within Front.
Because Front handles every channel — email, SMS, chat, and more — in one place, the AI assistant gets the full context of a conversation: messages across all channels, internal comments, tag and assignment history, and rule actions, all in one timeline.
Head to Front Community to read the [official announcement](https://community.front.com/announcements-63/front-s-mcp-server-bring-front-into-your-ai-workflows-3958) and get the [starter guide](https://community.front.com/workflows-discussion-47/front-mcp-server-starter-guide-plug-and-play-prompts-3964) with ready-to-use templates for the MCP.
---
## What is the MCP server?
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to external tools. The *MCP server* specifically enables external AI assistants and similar tools to access a predetermined set of Front data and actions. Connecting to the Front MCP server means the AI assistant can do things like search your inbox, read a thread, draft a reply, leave an internal comment, or tag a conversation — as you, with your permissions.
**Think of it as giving the AI assistant a key to Front that only works while you're authorized, and only does the things your role already allows.**
---
## What you can do with it
Here are some common ways to put the MCP server to work:
**Triage your inbox**
> "Look at my Open inbox and help me prioritize what to respond to first. Flag anything that mentions billing or churn risk."
**Draft higher quality replies with broader context**
> "Find the most recent conversation with [customer]. Cross-reference their account in Salesforce, then draft a reply that addresses their question and acknowledges where they are in the renewal cycle."
**Investigate a bug report**
> "Open the most recent conversation tagged 'bug.' Summarize the issue, search GitHub for related PRs, and post an internal comment for engineering with what you find."

title: Frontend MCP Server
snippet:
# Frontend MCP Server
The Frontend MCP server gives agents access to the parts of a project they can’t reach from the sandbox: its [Frontend Cloud](/cloud/overview) database, its media library, its deploy logs and environment variable names, image and video generation, Frontend’s build skills, and the [services the project has connected](/mcp/integrations). Every project has it, enabled by default.
```
https://mcp.frontend.co/mcp
```
## How agents use it
Section titled “How agents use it”
Instead of loading every action as a separate tool, the server offers four tools that let an agent find and run what it needs:
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `search_tools` | Finds the tools for a task, such as “query the database” or “list the store’s products”, and returns their input schemas and whether each service is connected. |
| `get_tool_schemas` | Returns the description and input schema of tools by name. |
| `multi_execute_tool` | Runs up to 20 tools at once, each with its arguments, and returns one result per call. |
| `list_connections` | Shows which services are connected, and to which account. |
Tool names combine the toolkit and the action, like `QUERY_DATABASE` or `SHOPIFY_LIST_PRODUCTS`. The agent’s own approval settings decide which calls need your confirmation: `multi_execute_tool` is marked as able to change data, and the other three as read-only.
## Frontend tools
Section titled “Frontend tools”
Frontend’s own tools are always available, with no connection needed:
| Tool | What it does | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `LIST_SKILLS`, `LOAD_SKILL` | List Frontend’s skills, instructions for building features like payments, a CMS, a database, a contact form or AI, and load one by name. | — |
| `GET_DATABASE_SCHEMA` | Lists the tables and columns of the project’s database. | The project’s [database](/cloud/database) |
| `QUERY_DATABASE` | Runs any SQL (SQLite dialect), including writes and schema changes, with optional parameters for `?` placeholders. | The project’s [database](/cloud/database) |
| `LIST_MEDIA`, `UPLOAD_MEDIA`, `DELETE_MEDIA` | List, upload (from a URL) and delete files in the project’s [media library](/cloud/storage). Returns each file’s public URL. | — |
| `GENERATE_IMAGE` | Generates or edits images from prompts, optionally with reference images, and saves them to the media library. | [OpenRouter](/integrations/openrouter) |
| `GENERATE_VIDEO` | Starts a video generation and returns a ticket. | [OpenRouter](/integrations/openrouter) |
|
